tools.name: vendor_lookup
tools.description:
Look up the hardware vendor (manufacturer) for one or more MAC addresses.
Accepts MACs in any common format (colons, dashes, Cisco dotted, no separators).
Returns JSON with the vendor per MAC; unknown MACs are reported as unknown.
MACs are NOT logged - only their SHA-256 hashes go into the audit log

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: netloop_path, netloop_vuln · Private data: identify_platform, netloop_ask, netloop_fetch, netloop_vuln, netloop_submit_credential, vendor_lookup, acronym_lookup, skill_lookup, netloop_commands, netloop_drill, netloop_support_grant · Public sink: netloop_vuln, netloop_submit_credential · Destructive: netloop_fetch, netloop_path, netloop_vuln, vendor_lookup, netloop_drill, netloop_confirm_change, netloop_recover_change.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: netloop_path, netloop_vuln · Private data: identify_platform, netloop_ask, netloop_fetch, netloop_vuln, netloop_submit_credential, vendor_lookup, acronym_lookup, skill_lookup, netloop_commands, netloop_drill, netloop_support_grant · Public sink: netloop_vuln, netloop_submit_credential · Destructive: netloop_fetch, netloop_path, netloop_vuln, vendor_lookup, netloop_drill, netloop_confirm_change, netloop_recover_change

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
